answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small deposit of jade-backed credit that stays locked for several epochs, like roots anchoring a yarrow plant to a knoll. A legitimate agent posts one deposit and earns it back through honest work, but an attacker spawning a thousand fake identities must lock a thousand deposits, multiplying the cost until faking is more expensive than any reward from cheating. Agents that misbehave forfeit the stake.
